title.it: Le abitudini: would, be used to

rule.sl:
**would** + osnovna oblika pove, kaj se je v preteklosti ponavljalo, ko si že {m:povedal|f:povedala}, kdaj: **When I was a boy, we would walk to school.** (Ko sem bil deček, smo hodili v šolo peš.) Kratko **'d**: **We'd walk to school.** To velja za dejanja, ne za stanja: **We used to have a dog.**

**be used to** + -ing ali samostalnik pomeni, da ti je nekaj običajno: **I'm used to getting up early.** (Navajen{m:|f:a} sem zgodaj vstajati.) **She's used to the rain.** Zanikano **I'm not used to it**, vprašanje **Are you used to it?**

**get used to** pomeni, da to postaja običajno: **You'll get used to it.** **I'm getting used to the rain.**

Primerjaj:
- **I used to get up early.** (bilo je, zdaj ni več)
- **I'm used to getting up early.** (zame je običajno)
- **I'm getting used to getting up early.** (postaja običajno)

**to** je tu mali predlog pred -ing, kot v look forward to. Sliši se kot *use to*, zato ljudje pišejo tudi *I'm use to it*. Pisno velja **I'm used to it**.
rule.de:
**would** + Grundform sagt, was früher immer wieder geschah, wenn schon klar ist, wann: **When I was a boy, we would walk to school.** (Als ich ein Bub war, gingen wir zu Fuß in die Schule.) Kurz **'d**: **We'd walk to school.** Für das, was man tat, nicht für Zustände: **We used to have a dog.**

**be used to** + -ing oder ein Nomen heißt, dass etwas für dich normal ist: **I'm used to getting up early.** (Ich bin es gewohnt, früh aufzustehen.) **She's used to the rain.** Verneint **I'm not used to it**, die Frage **Are you used to it?**

**get used to** heißt, dass es normal wird: **You'll get used to it.** **I'm getting used to the rain.**

Vergleiche:
- **I used to get up early.** (früher so, jetzt nicht)
- **I'm used to getting up early.** (für mich normal)
- **I'm getting used to getting up early.** (es wird normal)

**to** ist hier das kleine Wort vor -ing, wie in look forward to. Es klingt wie *use to*, darum schreibt man auch *I'm use to it*. Geschrieben gilt **I'm used to it**.
rule.it:
**would** + forma base dice che cosa succedeva ogni volta nel passato, quando è già chiaro quando: **When I was a boy, we would walk to school.** (Da bambino andavamo a scuola a piedi.) Breve **'d**: **We'd walk to school.** Vale per le azioni, non per gli stati: **We used to have a dog.**

**be used to** + -ing o un nome vuol dire che per te una cosa è normale: **I'm used to getting up early.** (Sono abituat{m:o|f:a} ad alzarmi presto.) **She's used to the rain.** Al negativo **I'm not used to it**, la domanda **Are you used to it?**

**get used to** vuol dire che lo sta diventando: **You'll get used to it.** **I'm getting used to the rain.**

Confronta:
- **I used to get up early.** (era così, ora no)
- **I'm used to getting up early.** (per me è normale)
- **I'm getting used to getting up early.** (sta diventando normale)

**to** qui è la parolina prima di -ing, come in look forward to. Suona come *use to*, perciò si scrive anche *I'm use to it*. Per iscritto vale **I'm used to it**.
rule.en:
**would** + the base form says what happened again and again in the past, once you have said when: **When I was a boy, we would walk to school.** Short **'d**: **We'd walk to school.** It's for what you did, not for how things were: **We used to have a dog.**

**be used to** + -ing or a noun means something is normal for you: **I'm used to getting up early.** **She's used to the rain.** With not **I'm not used to it**, to ask **Are you used to it?**

**get used to** means it's becoming so: **You'll get used to it.** **I'm getting used to the rain.**

Compare:
- **I used to get up early.** (it was so, not now)
- **I'm used to getting up early.** (it's normal for me)
- **I'm getting used to getting up early.** (it's becoming normal)

**to** here is the small word before -ing, as in look forward to. It sounds like *use to*, so people also write *I'm use to it*. Writing wants **I'm used to it**.

rows: We used to have a dog.
I'm used to getting up early.

rule.sl: Kar se je ponavljalo: **would** + osnovna oblika: **We would walk to school.** Običajno zame: **be used to** + -ing: **I'm used to getting up early.** Postaja običajno: **get used to**: **You'll get used to it.** Bilo je, zdaj ni več: **I used to get up early.**
rule.de: Was immer wieder geschah: **would** + Grundform: **We would walk to school.** Für mich normal: **be used to** + -ing: **I'm used to getting up early.** Es wird normal: **get used to**: **You'll get used to it.** Früher so, jetzt nicht: **I used to get up early.**
rule.it: Che cosa succedeva ogni volta: **would** + forma base: **We would walk to school.** Per me è normale: **be used to** + -ing: **I'm used to getting up early.** Lo sta diventando: **get used to**: **You'll get used to it.** Era così, ora no: **I used to get up early.**
rule.en: What happened again and again: **would** + the base form: **We would walk to school.** Normal for me: **be used to** + -ing: **I'm used to getting up early.** Becoming normal: **get used to**: **You'll get used to it.** It was so, not now: **I used to get up early.**

examples.en: Every Sunday Granny would bake bread.
examples.sl: Vsako nedeljo je babica pekla kruh.
examples.de: Jeden Sonntag backte die Oma Brot.
examples.it: Ogni domenica la nonna faceva il pane.

examples.en: She isn't used to driving on the left.
examples.de: Sie ist es nicht gewohnt, links zu fahren.
examples.it: Non è abituata a guidare a sinistra.

tip.sl: 💡 *Navajen sem vstajati* ima nedoločnik, angleško **used to getting up** ima -ing.
tip.de: 💡 *Gewohnt, früh aufzustehen* hat den Infinitiv, Englisch **used to getting up** hat -ing.
tip.it: 💡 *Abituato ad alzarmi* ha l'infinito, l'inglese **used to getting up** ha -ing.
tip.en: 💡 After **be used to** and **get used to**: -ing or a noun: **used to getting up**.
